## S037  ·  Espinoza V, Viers JH (2024). The paradox of production: Surface water supply drives agricultural productivity but not prosperity in California's San Joaquin Valley. PLOS Water 3(6): e0000192.

- **Stored:** `sample_size` = "153 (97 ID-DAC + 56 GDC census places)".
- **What the PDF shows:** The PDF never prints 153 (searched the whole text layer). It prints the two group sizes, n = 97 and n = 56, and the stored 153 is their sum, an AI-derived total. Every other stored number (83% vs 79%, p = 0.1363; 83% vs 81%, p = 0.3147; $34,276 vs $36,450, p = 0.7893) is printed in Table 1.
  - *Table 1 header (p. 13)*: "Socioeconomic Variable (mean) ID-DAC (n = 97) GDC (n = 56) P-Value (α = 0.05)"
  - *Table 1 rows (p. 13)*: "Poor Drinking Water Exposure (%) 83 79 0.1363 Overall DAC Vulnerability (%) 83 81 0.3147"
  - *Table 1, income row (p. 13)*: "$34,276 $36,450 0.7893"
  - *Text (p. 13)*: "this paper compares DACs within irrigation district boundaries (n = 97), hereafter ID DACs, and DACs in GDCs (n = 56), hereafter GDCs"
  - *Search for 153 (whole text layer, plain and layout)*: no match.
- **Proposed correction (not applied):** `sample_size` -> "97 ID-DAC census places and 56 GDC census places (n = 97 and n = 56; Table 1, p. 13)" (drop the derived total 153).

## S470  ·  Amorim, D.P.d.L., Resende, M., Miranda, R.J.S. & Freistadt, J. (2025). The effect of the regulation and regulatory enforcement on the implementation of the social tariff in the water sector: empirical

- **Stored:** `effect_estimate` = "... ~13-13.5 percentage-point effect (0-1 scaled index)" (13.5 not found); the main estimates +19.21, +19.16 and +18.82 are stored rounded.
- **What the PDF shows:** Table 5 prints the main estimates to four decimals (19.2078 with SE 0.8174; 19.155 with 0.8143; 18.819 with 0.8101) and the stored +19.21, +19.16, +18.82 and SE 0.8174 are those numbers rounded or copied. The robustness estimates are printed on the 0 to 1 scale (0.1345, 0.1348, 0.1313; SE 0.0059, 0.0059, 0.0060) and the text says 'about a 13% increase'. The stored '13-13.5 percentage points' is those coefficients times 100 and rounded up (13.45, 13.48, 13.13); 13.5 itself is never printed.
  - *Table 5, REGU row (p. 16)*: "REGU 19.2078*** 0.8174 19.155*** 0.8143 18.819*** 0.8101"
  - *Table 6, REGU row (p. 18)*: "REGU 0.1345*** 0.0059 0.1348*** 0.0059 0.1313*** 0.0060"
  - *Text on the robustness check (p. 17)*: "In the robustness check models, the effect of the regulation and enforcement on the implementation of the social tariff is about a 13% increase."
- **Proposed correction (not applied):** `effect_estimate`: replace "a smaller but still significant ~13-13.5 percentage-point effect (0-1 scaled index)" with "a smaller but still significant effect: REGU 0.1345 (SE 0.0059), 0.1348 (0.0059) and 0.1313 (0.0060) on the 0-1 index (Table 6, p. 18), 'about a 13% increase' (p. 17)"; optionally give the main estimates as printed (19.2078, 19.155, 18.819).
